title: Time Series Atlas
status: Eight investigations executed and independently reviewed
question: Which time series methods answer useful questions once source conventions, information timing, and evaluation assumptions are made explicit?
one_liner: Question-led time series studies with visible critiques, verified corrections and reproducible evidence.
aim: Demonstrate analytical judgment through reproducible investigations and short process stories, with independent agent reviews before design, execution, and publication.
scope: Seven real-data investigations—CO₂, electricity, retail, oil, river flow, air quality and ECG—plus synthetic change-detection and sampling controls. Each includes a frozen design, retained results, figures, review evidence and a plain-language process story.
conclusion: Useful answers depend on the question and evaluation: zero forecasts can win sparse-sales error while missing volume, high-day river recall can hide missed new rises, and high ECG accuracy can conceal rare-class failure.

summary.question: What changes when we challenge the question, measurements, and evaluation before trusting a time series result?
summary.result: The collection shows how data provenance, information timing, metric choice and independence assumptions change the answer.

headline.label: Three-year December CO₂ MAE, recent growth
ECG forest macro F1, four groups

finding: In the fixed electricity panel, the shared model worsened forecasts for {{test.pooled_worse_customers:d}} customers. For three-year December targets, recent-growth CO₂ regression reduced MAE from {{co2_fixed:.3f}} to {{co2_recent:.3f}} ppm; these are revised-data hindcasts.
An always-zero retail forecast won normalized absolute error while missing every recorded sale. TSB won raw-unit error. Metric weighting and the decision being supported changed the interpretation.

Adaptive oil variance forecasts beat the fixed baseline on QLIKE while direction forecasts lost to prevalence on Brier. A secondary variance loss reversed the ranking. Same-hour air-quality peers outperformed local persistence under simulated outages, with scoring limited by observed truth.

River high-day recall did not translate into equally high new-onset recall. Past weather added little at the longer date offset and brought more false-alert episodes; daily information assumptions limit warning claims.

The ECG forest scored {{ecg_forest:.3f}} macro F1 versus the majority baseline’s {{ecg_majority:.3f}}, yet missed every fusion-group beat. Expert beat locations were supplied and people were kept apart during evaluation.

Synthetic controls expose two different failures: persistent noise breaks frozen alert calibration, while regular thinning leaves equally strong frequency aliases. A clear peak is not proof of unique identification.

The process story preserves initial design risks, later source discrepancies, actual code and copy defects, missed review findings, and verified corrections. Agent agreement is not independent human validation.

traps.how: Features use only observations available at each declared origin; future-perturbation checks test that earlier predictions remain unchanged.
Power and interval labels are explicit. Provider DST conventions differ from sampled values, so calendar masks and a nominal-clock assumption are recorded.
Comparison designs were committed before fitting, with no model selection on final scores. Customer differences and sensitivity results remain visible.

figures.caption: A zero sales forecast has the lowest normalized absolute error while missing all recorded volume. Raw-unit error gives a different ranking.
Class-specific recall and variation across held-out people expose failures hidden by pooled accuracy. Per-person denominators include only present classes.
High-day and eligible-onset recall use different cohorts and weighting. False alerts and misses in the linked report qualify these daily date-offset comparisons.
Frequency recovery and equal-power aliases answer different questions. The regular thinning control remains nonidentifiable under the declared search.

not_claimed: Universal model rankings, causal attribution, latent retail demand, realized savings or clinical benefit.
Operational reporting latency, an automatic ECG detector, or generalization to unobserved catchments.
Guaranteed future recovery of unchanged oil inputs; they require explicit free acquisition and are not mirrored.
Independent human validation or completion of conditional advanced-method extensions.

verification.harness: Offline invariant tests; analysis evidence linked in each report

data: EIA oil series with third-party attribution; fetch-only inputs
